summary: Validated the GPS jitter suppression fix in /app/backend/routes/mobile.py::_apply_location_fix. Two new mechanisms verified: (A) EXIT DEBOUNCE — a single outside live-location fix now returns 'exit_pending' (status stays 'active') and NO pause_live log entry is added; only a second outside fix beyond EXIT_GRACE_MS (3min) confirms the exit and writes a BACKDATED pause_live crossing at the first-outside ts_ms. Grace-window outside time is NOT counted toward total_inside_ms. (B) IMPOSSIBLE-SPEED FILTER — a fix implying >55 m/s over <=120s with >=100m displacement returns outcome 'rejected_gps_glitch', leaves session state (status + last_fix) untouched, and writes no gps_ping / no log entry. Also confirmed the /location-sync offline batch path drains through the same debounce/speed logic in ts_ms order without error, and idempotent replay still works via the last_live_ts_ms watermark. Coverage-gap regression still passes. 8/8 tests green.
critical_code_review_comments: mobile.py:636-670 exit debounce is implemented cleanly: first-outside stashes pending_exit_ms; subsequent inside fix clears it (was_pending flag skips dt accrual over the excursion span) and no log entry is written; a second outside beyond EXIT_GRACE_MS backdates paused_at + pause_live.ts_ms to the initial outside — matches spec.
mobile.py:619-626 speed filter runs BEFORE gps_pings.insert_one (line 629) so rejected spikes leave no trail, correct.

One minor nit: the speed filter still returns before updating last_live_ts_ms, so a legitimate very-fast movement (e.g., driving) that happens to trip the threshold once will be silently dropped and the next fix compared against the previous, potentially compounding rejections. Not a blocker for the current scenario but worth logging metrics on for tuning.

The offline /location-sync path (line 764) processes each fix through _apply_location_fix serially in ts order — the exit-debounce state (pending_exit_ms in DB) survives fix-to-fix within the same batch, so a batch containing two outside fixes >3min apart correctly confirms the exit. Verified in TestOfflineBatchReplayAccrual.

Watermark check at mobile.py:530 protects replay idempotency but does NOT protect against a rejected_gps_glitch not updating last_live_ts_ms — that is intentional (a legit next fix should still be evaluated); acceptable.
